title: Gateway authz validators must read resource IDs from the parsed proto message, not raw request params
answers: gateway secret delete or update acts on the wrong secret when request mixes snake_case and camelCase fields
AI Gateway permission check ignores secretId or endpointId alias in the request body
403 or wrong-resource authorization for gateway endpoints or model definitions sent with JSON-name keys
why does gateway permission check read secret_id differently from the handler
body:
Symptom: a user sends a gateway request whose resource ID uses a camelCase alias (e.g. secretId) alongside a snake_case key, and authorization is evaluated against a different resource than the handler uses.
Root cause: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_get_permission_from_gateway_secret_id (and the endpoint/model-definition equivalents) read raw keys via _get_request_param("secret_id"), which misses protobuf JSON-name aliases.
Fix pattern: in each validate_can_*_gateway_* validator, parse with _get_request_message(<RequestProto>()) and use msg.<field>; then call the shared helper (_get_gateway_secret_permission, _get_gateway_endpoint_permission, _get_gateway_model_definition_permission) with that value. Keep the helpers taking an explicit ID so the raw-param path is not reused.
Constraints: applies to gateway routes registered in the before-request validator map. A GET by name has no ID in the message, so resolve endpoint_id via _get_tracking_store().get_gateway_endpoint(name=...) first. Do not add local try/except there; the outer @catch_mlflow_exception turns MlflowException into the proper error response.
applies: Any gateway (secrets, model definitions, endpoints, guardrail/binding routes) authorization validator in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py.
says: Updating or deleting a gateway secret fails with a permission error when using camelCase fields.
Gateway permission checks evaluate the wrong resource when requests use alternative identifier field names.
Users receive an unauthorized error when managing gateway endpoints with JSON style property names.
Ensure authorization checks for gateway secrets correctly identify resources across different request formats.
Modifying a gateway model definition targets the wrong resource during permission evaluation.
search: AI Gateway authorization validators in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py must obtain resource IDs from parsed protobuf request messages rather than raw request parameters. Reading raw parameters via _get_request_param misses protobuf JSON-name aliases like secretId or endpointId, causing permission checks to evaluate a different resource than the handler uses. Validators must parse requests with _get_request_message and pass msg.<field> to explicit helpers (_get_gateway_secret_permission, _get_gateway_endpoint_permission, _get_gateway_model_definition_permission). For GET requests by name where the message lacks an ID, endpoint_id is resolved via _get_tracking_store().get_gateway_endpoint(name=...) without local try/except, delegating errors to @catch_mlflow_exception.
